text: Normal delivery should complete within 2 hours of the water sac appearing. If delivery is delayed, a pelvic exam should assess cervical dilation, fetal position, and whether correction is possible. Normal fetal position is front feet pointing out, right-side up, with the chin resting on the forelegs; abnormal positions include backwards presentation, one or more front legs held back, or the head turned back. An oversized fetus is rare in Cambodia, but if a calf has died in the uterus, gas quickly builds under its skin, increasing its size — ropes tied to the legs may be needed to pull it out. When the cow is weak or in poor condition, contractions may not be strong enough; 50 IU (5 ml) of oxytocin can strengthen contractions.
